So He said, linking it to what is implied by the supposed phrase, "Mention this, for it suffices for the purpose of everyone possessed of intellect": ﴿And when﴾; that is, and mention the saying of your Lord when; ﴿your Lord said﴾; that is, the One who has been good to you by honouring your father Adam (peace be upon him), for your honour; ﴿to the angels﴾. Since this is something that could be doubted, He emphasised it and said: ﴿Indeed, I am going to create a human being﴾; that is, a living creature not clothed in skin, with the nature He placed upon it in human form; ﴿from clay﴾; that is, clay of hard dryness; ﴿from black mud﴾; that is, black, foul-smelling clay; ﴿molded﴾; that is, shaped into the form of a human being in its hollows and its limbs, as if it were poured into a mould. Al-Rummani said: its root meaning is continuing in one direction, from their saying "in a single course" (ʿalā sanan wāḥid);

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 29:

﴿So when I have proportioned him﴾; i.e., I made him balanced, completed him, and prepared him for the breathing of the spirit (al-nafkh al-ruh), a preparation close to the act itself; ﴿and breathed into him of My spirit﴾; i.e., I created life in him (p-54), just as fire catches the wick by blowing; and this is a figurative expression (tamthil). He attributed the spirit to Himself as an honour; it is that by which the body becomes alive. More noble than this is that by which the spirit becomes knowing; and more noble than that is that by which the knower becomes one who acts, humble in awe; ﴿so fall down before him﴾; i.e., in exaltation, while you are ﴿prostrating﴾; i.e., prostrate to him with the prostration of one who hastens to it and yields readily, as if it had occurred without his choice.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 30:

﴿So the angels prostrated, all of them together﴾; i.e., by reason of this command, without any hesitation, when the time came that I had commanded them concerning that human being, who is your father Adam (peace be upon him), while you were in his loins, ﴿all of them together﴾.

When al-Biqa'i had gone to the utmost in emphasizing what the plural form conveyed, he made an exception, saying: ﴿except Iblis﴾. It was said (and it was also said: rather, because he was one among them, attached to them, working by their deeds, he was included among them, so it was as if he were one of them, and therefore his exception was valid on that basis; so it is as if it were said: "What did he do?" And it was answered, to magnify his opposition: ﴿he refused to be among those who prostrate﴾ — that is, because of a harshness in his nature; ﴿among those who prostrate﴾ [al-Hijr: 98]). Or it is because He did not say "so he refused" with a conjunction (fa-), since the exception is disjunctive (munqati'), for Iblis was from fire, while the angels were from light, and they do not eat, nor drink, nor marry, unlike him.

Then it is as if it were said: "What did the King do to him?" It is said: He did not hasten to punish him; rather (p-55) He deferred him until his appointed term, which was decreed for him from eternity, just as He did not hasten to punish you for that. Then it is as if it were said: "What did He say to him?" It is said: ﴿He said﴾ to him, in order to establish the proof against him before the creatures outwardly, just as the proof was previously established against him in knowledge inwardly: ﴿O Iblis﴾. He chose this name here, because al-iblas (dejection) means despair of all good, stillness and brokenness, sorrow and bewilderment, cutting off of argument, and remorse. ﴿What is wrong with you?﴾ That is, what excuse do you have for ﴿not being⁠﴾ — that is, with your heart and your body — ﴿among those who prostrate﴾, to One whom I commanded you to prostrate to, while you know, from what I possess of greatness and majesty, what most of creation does not know?

"He said, 'I would never prostrate myself to a human, whom You created from clay, from black mud molded into shape.'"

Wait—I should translate faithfully, not paraphrase. Let me produce the actual translation.

He said: "I was not" — and he emphasized it to show his persistence and to express his arrogance (al-kibr) — so he said: ﴿I will not prostrate to a mortal﴾; that is, one of apparent body, having no capacity for change and transformation; ﴿whom You created from clay﴾; that is, dry clay, with no resistance in it, rather when it is struck it responds with a sound; ﴿from black mud﴾; that is, altered clay, dark and turbid; ﴿molded﴾; that is, shaped into the form of pottery, prepared for rubbing, not repelling the hand of one who touches it; "and I am better than him, because You created me from fire, beneficial through its radiance, refusing to whoever wants to burn with it; so my submission to him contradicts my condition, and it is impossible for me; and obliging me to it is injustice."

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 34:**

So it is as if it were said: "What was his answer?" It was said: ﴿He said: Then get out﴾; meaning: as a consequence of your arrogance (p-56), I say to you: get out ﴿from it﴾; meaning: from the abode of holiness (Dar al-Qudus). It was said: from the heaven; and it was said: from the Garden. ﴿For you are accursed﴾; meaning: expelled, since (this is not said except of one who is far off, for whom an increase in his distance is desired; indeed, his destruction). The reason for the expulsion is that it is an abode in which no arrogant, disobedient one who opposes My command may dwell, for to Me belongs the executing decree and the perfect greatness that necessitates the obligation of obedience. It is not fitting for one whom I commanded with what has passed to hold back from My command, let alone to strike examples for Me and confront Me with disputation, impugning what belongs to Me of majesty and beauty.

Then he confirmed his distance by informing of its continuation, so he said: ﴿And upon you is the curse﴾; that is, specifically; ﴿the curse﴾; that is, the complete one; because of the decree of directly causing the means of distance; ﴿until the Day of Judgment﴾; that is, until the day when obligation ends and the dawn of recompense rises, with the passing away of all creation; and the lapse of the period in which repentance is valid, which is the means of nearness. This is an indication of the perpetuity of expulsion and the successive continuation of distance and abhorrence. Thus, in this period one cannot accomplish any deed that would be a cause of nearness to the presence of intimacy and the court of holiness. And whoever (at its time) knows with certainty that he will not be forgiven, he is punished forever.

When this (the verse's words) made clear that his curse would endure, because he had been barred from drawing near (to God) in the abode of action, while what comes after that is the place of recompense and not of action, and because this implied that he was granted respite up to that limit, and its outward meaning was that his curse was intended by it, it was as though it was said: "What did he say when he heard that?" So it was said: ﴿He said﴾, mentioning the attribute of beneficence and the means of asking for respite: ﴿My Lord﴾. Thus he acknowledged servitude and God's beneficence toward him, and this did not lead him to repentance, since (the verse) judges that his curse is permanent. Therefore no one who hopes for the faith of one sealed in disbelief should expect that his request will be granted. He used the particle of causation (fa) because respite had been understood from the words "granting time," so he said: ﴿So grant me respite﴾. Al-inzar (respite) is the postponement of one who needs time to consider his affair, ﴿until the day they are raised﴾. He took the Day of Religion (yawm al-din) in its literal sense, and intended to state explicitly the respite granted to him, so that he would be safe from death.
So it is as if it were said: "What was said to him?" It was said: ﴿He said﴾; his Lord said to him: ﴿Indeed you are﴾; that is, because of the judgment that has preceded; ﴿among those reprieved﴾;

Al-Biqa'i said: He cut short what he had embellished of deception; so he said: ﴿Until﴾. Since "the day" is that in which a clear matter is completed, and the awesome days were three — the time of the death of the living who had come out of the Abode of Eternity; then the raising of the dead; then the separation between them by settling each group in its abode — He said: ﴿the day﴾. Since "the time" is the most indicative of the words for time with respect to a term (ajal), he said: ﴿of the time﴾. And since he had embellished in this request of his an embellishment that gave the impression of his ignorance of the inevitability of death for every responsible person (mukallaf), He (Exalted) made clear that it is among what is not unknown, so He said: ﴿the appointed﴾; that is, the time in which I have decreed death for you, and it is the first blast (al-nafkhah al-ula), and what follows it of the death of every creature that was not in the Abode of Eternity.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 39:

When the ruling regarding his misguiding [of mankind], as we have said, was understood from what preceded, the listener was as if he had asked: "So what did he say?" It was answered: ﴿He said﴾, attributing himself to the Worshipped, the Exalted, who is not questioned about what He does, and all of whose actions are justice and wisdom, after he had elevated himself above the human servant: ﴿My Lord﴾, that is, O Originator and Nurturer of me; ﴿and by Your might﴾; ﴿because You have led me astray﴾, that is, because of Your leading me astray on account of them. For the sake of emphasizing this cause, he placed it before the answer to the oath, which indicates what is sworn by, and that answer is his saying: ﴿I will surely make [evil] attractive to them﴾, that is, an enormous making-attractive of the disobediences and of the permissible things that lead to them, which occupy one from obedience and divert one from it; ﴿on earth﴾, that is, the place of heedlessness, of which they are a part, and a thing inclines toward what is part of it. Thus, by this reading, it is equivalent to the verse in Surah Sad: "then by Your might" (﴿فَبِعِزَّتِكَ﴾). Tazyin (making-attractive, adornment) is the making of a thing acceptable to the soul, from the standpoint of natural disposition and intellect, whether in truth or in falsehood; ﴿and I will surely lead them all astray﴾, that is, into misguidance away from the praiseworthy path; ﴿all of them﴾, as retribution against myself.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 40:

﴿Except Your servants among them﴾; i.e., those honored by being attributed to You; for this reason they do not incline away from You toward anything other than You. Therefore He (Iblis) excepted from them ﴿the sincere ones (al-mukhlasin)﴾. Thus he increased in misguidance by this speech; and he was not able to say instead of that: "My Lord, turn to me in forgiveness," and the like of supplication, as Adam, peace be upon him, said when gentleness enveloped him and pardon overtook him. So hold fast to this blessing. And "ikhlas" (sincerity, i.e., singling out a thing from whatever else mixes with it): the isolation of a thing from what else may be mixed into it.

Then it is as if it were said: "By what is he answered?" It was said: ﴿He said﴾; God; in His reply, refuting what his speech had given the impression of, namely that he has an action that is self-sufficient; contradicting him: ﴿This﴾; that is: what you have mentioned of the condition of the one exempted and the one from whom he is exempted; ﴿is a path upon Me, straight﴾; because I have decreed it, even if you had not said it; and I have judged it against you and against them; so there is no escape for you from it. It is as if it were said: upon Me is its establishment; or it is: it leads to Me, that there is no crookedness for its travelers away from returning to Me and passing by Me; meaning that no one can do anything without My will; for I am on the watch (bil-mirsad).

Then he explained that by his saying, adding all the servants to Himself as is the reality, and negating what the speech might suggest, that Iblis has an independent action: ﴿Indeed, My servants﴾; that is, generally. ﴿You have no authority over them﴾; that is, in any way whatsoever. ﴿Over them is no authority﴾; that is, to turn them all away from what pleases Me. ﴿except those who follow you﴾; that is, deliberately, out of their own intent and desire to follow you, ﴿of the deviators﴾; and who die without repentance. For indeed I have made for you authority over them through embellishment and seduction.

It has also been said, and this is evident, that the idafah (annexation of "My servants") is for honour, so it includes only the sincere ones (al-khullas). In that case the istithna' (exception) is munqati' (disjunctive). The benefit of framing it in the form of an exception, on the assumption of disjunction, is encouragement toward the rank of honour through being attributed to Him, and turning away from following the enemy toward turning to Him, because people of noble souls and lofty aspirations compete for that station and regard it, as is the truth, as the highest goal.
And indeed, Hell is their appointed place—﴿Indeed, Hell is their appointed meeting-place, all of them﴾; that is, the misguided ones: Iblis and whoever followed him, ﴿all of them﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 44:

Then he made clear that they (the people of the Fire) differ in it (in their ranks). So He said: ﴿It has seven gates﴾. Al-Rummani said: They are layers (tiers), one above another. This is related from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ibn Jurayj (may Allah have mercy on them). ﴿For each gate of them﴾: that is, of the deviators specifically, in which no one who is sincere shares with them. ﴿Is an allotted portion﴾: known to Us from eternity, by Our decree of it, neither increasing anything nor decreasing anything. There is no action in it except through the causal means which We have made apparent, so that We may tie the rulings to them according to what your intellects and the courses of your customs require. It is related from Ibn Jurayj that the highest is Jahannam, then Laza, then al-Hutamah, then al-Sa'ir, then Saqar, then al-Jahim, then al-Hawiyah. In one copy, Saqar is placed before Laza. And it is related from al-Dahhak that the highest is for the People of Monotheism, from which they (eventually) come out; the second is for the Christians, the third for the Jews, the fourth for the Sabians, the fifth for the Magians, the sixth for the polytheists of the Arabs, and the seventh for the hypocrites. The reason for their ascending order is the difference in the types of disbelief in severity and lightness. ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf: 49], out of His mercy, glory be to Him.

Perhaps they were seven in terms of the categories of disbelievers, for they are either deniers (muʿattilah) or affirmers (muthbitah). The affirmers are either Jews, or Sabians, or Christians, or Magians, or worshippers of idols. And all of them are either open (declared) disbelievers or hypocrites. Since the hypocrite is not known outwardly as to which of these he is, he was counted as one category, and his matter in distinguishing him was left to the All-Knowing, the All-Aware. And since all of them act by what Allah has not permitted, they were in the ruling of the deniers, because they describe Allah with other than His attribute. So the categories returned to six, and the disobedient (ʿusat) of every group were added to them. Thus the portion of the highest tier of the Fire was made to correspond to the category of hypocrites of every nation, because they do the deeds of disbelievers while professing faith, just as the deeds of the hypocrites are the deeds of believers while concealing disbelief. So they were the most concealed of the disbelievers, and therefore they have the lowest level of the Fire.

Then I saw in "Rashf al-Nasa'ih al-Iymaniyyah wa Kashf al-Fada'ih al-Yunaniyyah" by the knower of Allah (exalted is He), Shihab al-Din ʿUmar ibn Muhammad al-Suhrawardi (may Allah have mercy on him), that they were made seven according to the seven limbs: the eye, the ear, the tongue, the belly, the private part, the hand, and the foot, because they are the sources of evil deeds. So their points of entry became the seven gates. This is taken from the book "al-Muhasabah" from the Ihya' of the Imam al-Ghazali. And since these same limbs are the sources of good deeds, on condition of intention, and intention is one of the deeds of the heart, the limbs increased by one, so the gates of the Gardens were made eight. This is the meaning of his saying: "He said: And the deeds of the hearts are not held to account for evil deeds."

When he mentioned the disbelievers, what had drawn them into misguidance, and what had emboldened them toward ugly deeds, he mentioned the sincere ones (al-mukhlisīn). Emphasizing the denial of those who deny the Resurrection, he said: ﴿Indeed, the God-conscious (al-muttaqūn)﴾; i.e., those firmly rooted in this attribute. And "al-muttaqī" (the God-conscious person) is one who makes faith, through its sincerity, a barrier between himself and punishment: ﴿in gardens and springs﴾ (p-٦٣)

Since a dwelling is only pleasant with safety, companionship, and security, He (Exalted is He) said: ﴿Enter it﴾; that is, it is said to them this; ﴿in peace﴾; that is, free from every calamity, welcomed by Us, and greeted upon entering; ﴿secure﴾ from all of that forever.

When the intimacy could not be complete except through kinship of kind, along with perfect affection and the purity of hearts from turbidity, He said: ﴿And We shall remove﴾; that is, by what We possess of greatness; ﴿whatever rancor is in their breasts﴾; that is, hatred that festers (yanghul), meaning it becomes lodged in the heart, while they are ﴿brothers﴾; that is, sincerely united; while they are ﴿on thrones﴾, the plural of "sarir" (couch), which is an elevated seat prepared for joy; ﴿facing one another﴾, so that no one sees the back of another. At the end of ath-Thaqafiyyat, it is related from al-Junayd, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: "How sweet is gathering with companions! And how bitter is gathering with opponents!"

Since the consideration turns to permanence and final outcome after that, He said: ﴿They shall not be touched therein by any fatigue﴾, that is, exhaustion, weariness, toil, and hardship; ﴿nor shall they be removed from it﴾. And since the true grievance in everything is only compulsion, He built the verb in the passive form in His saying ﴿removed﴾ (bi-mukhrajeena, "being made to leave"), [keeping the Arabic word بِمُخْرَجِينَ (bi-mukhrajīn) in mind].

Since the implication of this context is that the one who is saved is only the God-fearing, the sincere (al-mukhlas), the one over whom Satan has no authority; and since the meaning of "sincere" (al-mukhlas) is one in whom there is no admixture of fault; and since man is a locus of deficiency; and since his falling into deficiency is incompatible with fulfilling the right of God-consciousness (taqwa) and sincerity; and since this might have made him despair of happiness, [God] necessitated for him persistence in distance. He - glory be to Him - said, in answer to one who seemed to ask: "What is the state of one who has not fulfilled the right of God-consciousness?":

﴿Inform My servants﴾; that is, inform them with a grand announcement; ﴿that I am I﴾; that is, Myself alone; ﴿the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾; that is, the One whose erasing of sins and whose honoring of whomever He wills, in all that He wills, encompasses everything; no one has any objection against Him.

Since that (perhaps) became a cause of the delusion that leads to persistence, He (Exalted is He) said: ﴿And that My punishment is He, the painful punishment﴾; that is, He alone is the painful punishment; that is, the most complete in causing pain. Thus it is known that the first (the forgiveness) is for the one who seeks forgiveness, and the second (the punishment) is for the one who persists. And it is understood from this that the God-conscious (al-muttaqun) entered Paradise only by His pardon, and the deviators (al-ghawun) were punished only by His justice. This is a "laff wa nashr" (a rhetorical device of folding and unfolding, in which several items are mentioned together and then each is matched back to its counterpart) that is "mushawwash" (scrambled, its correspondences not in the order of the first mention), according to what is most eloquent.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 51:

When He (glorified is He) had completed the explanation of His saying: ﴿That they may know that He is but one God﴾ [Ibrahim: 52], and what followed it of indication of the Resurrection, He began to explain ﴿and that people of understanding may take heed﴾ [Ibrahim: 52], with the story of the Friend (al-Khalil, i.e., Abraham) — peace be upon him — and what follows it, while fulfilling the mention of the Return (al-ma'ad, the Resurrection): sometimes by allusion (p-65) and sometimes by explicit statement; and deterring from presumption in seeking the coming of the angels — peace be upon them; and turning to His saying: ﴿Praise be to God, who has granted me, in old age, Isma'il and Ishaq﴾ [Ibrahim: 39]; in a style explaining what this story was followed by. For the occurrence of despair is a cause for the verse of forgiveness, and the report of the punishment of the nations is an illustration for the verse of punishment, so that those addressed may be restrained. He singled out for them the mention of those who are nearest to their lands from among the punished whom they know, because that is more striking to the soul. So He said (exalted is He): ﴿And inform them﴾; that is: tell them with a great telling; ﴿about the guests of Abraham﴾. The "guest" (al-dayf) is one who joins another seeking hospitality; these were named with this name because they were in the form of guests. Thus it is from the indication of inclusion (dalalat al-tadammun).

ۚ﴿When they entered upon him﴾; that is, Ibrahim (peace be upon him), ﴿and said﴾; that is, immediately upon entering, ﴿"Peace!"﴾

Since their request in this form was addressed to the angels in a manner more emphatic than what is in Surah Hud (peace be upon him), he indicated to them the fear that comes from seeing the angels, even if they were bringers of good tidings and in the best form of human appearance, by his saying: ﴿"Indeed, we are fearful of you"﴾; by the language of state or of speech; ﴿"Indeed"﴾; that is, I and those with me; ﴿"we are fearful of you"﴾. He omitted mention of their reply with peace. This does not conflict with what is in Surah Hud and elsewhere (p-66) where it is mentioned, for "idh" is a temporal adverb meaning "when/at the time that," and "al-hin" (the time) may be broad, so that what occurs within it is sometimes mentioned in its entirety in its order, sometimes in other than that order, and sometimes only part of it is mentioned with some part omitted, while all aspects of the report remain true, because the whole was comprising all of it. These variations in these ways are for meanings that Allah grants to whoever He wills to extract them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 53:

When he informed them that he had told them of his apprehension (wajal) concerning them, the listener became eager for their reply. So He said: ﴿They said﴾, intending to reassure him: ﴿Do not be apprehensive﴾. Wajal (al-wajal) is the disturbance of the soul in anticipation of what is disliked. Then they gave the reason for that, in their words, emphasizing in order to uproot what was in his soul of apprehension, which contradicts good tidings: ﴿Indeed, We give you good news of a boy﴾, that is, a child, a male, who is in the utmost strength, and is not like the children of the elderly who are weak. And since his fear was due to the concealment of their matter from him, the attribute of knowledge carried a particular distinction in this context, so they said: ﴿knowing﴾.

Then it is as if it were said: "So what did he say?" It was answered: ﴿He said﴾, displaying amazement, wishing to confirm the matter and to emphasize it: ﴿Do you give me good news﴾; that is, of that [matter]; ﴿despite old age having touched me﴾; that is, the old age with which there is no vitality by which a child could come from him. Or [is it] despite my returning to youth? For this reason he made his next words a consequence of this: ﴿Then by what do you give me good news?﴾; explain that to me with a clear and satisfying explanation.

(p-67) ﴿They said: "We have brought you the glad tidings of the truth"﴾; i.e., the matter that is established and certain, decisively settled, that will inevitably come to pass, which corresponds to our report; ﴿so do not be among the despairing﴾; i.e., because of our giving you the glad tidings of the truth; ﴿among the despairing﴾; i.e., those who lose hope, who have settled into their despair, saying things similar to their sayings.

When they had kindled his alarm with this prohibition, [Ibrahim] said, disapproving that he should be among those who despair: "And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord, except those who are astray?" (Qur'an 15:56). That is, who despairs of this despair, of the mercy of his Lord, whose beneficence has never ceased to flow upon him, except the astray, i.e., those who stray from the path of correct belief concerning their Lord, which is part of the completeness of His power, and that He is not harmed by disobedience nor benefited by obedience. This is an indication that he was not despairing; rather he was seeking to verify the report. And in this there is an allusion to the matter of the Return (ma'ad).

When the good news was confirmed, and he saw them coming together in a form other than the one in which the angel comes down with revelation, and he and others among the knowers of God, aware that the angels are only sent down with truth, this was a reason for him to ask them about their business, so that all his fear might leave him. Therefore ﴿He said, "Then what is your business"﴾, with the fa' of causation, ﴿khatbukum﴾ (your affair). Abu Hayyan said: "al-khatb" (affair) is hardly ever used except of a grave matter, end of quote. Al-Rummani said: it is a momentous matter. ﴿O messengers﴾, for you have come only for a great matter that will be a decisive distinction between the doomed and the saved.

They said, "Indeed, we have been sent" (﴿قالوا إنا﴾). Since he (Lot) knew who had sent them, they used the passive form for their statement: ﴿أُرْسِلْنا﴾ ("we have been sent"); that is, by the sending of the Mighty, the Wise, whom you (Lot) are the most knowledgeable of people in this age about. ﴿To a people﴾; that is, people possessing might and protection; ﴿criminal﴾; that is, deeply immersed in wrongdoing, all of them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 59:

When their sending was for the punishment, they said, making an exception from the pronoun in "criminals" (mujrimin); that is, they had all committed a great crime, ﴿except the family of Lot﴾; so they excepted them from being criminals, which necessitates that they were not sent to punish them. This moved the soul to ask about their condition, for they were among those on whose account the sending had taken place. So they answered with their saying: ﴿Indeed, we will surely deliver them﴾; that is, with a great deliverance, through the gradual progression of causes in the customary way; ﴿all of them﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 60:

﴿Except his wife﴾; so when they excluded her from those they would save, her matter was open to being that she would be punished, and to being that God (exalted is He) would save her on account of others. The soul became eager to learn what God had decreed concerning that. So it was said, by attributing the verb to themselves (because of their special relationship with the One who decrees, glorified is He): ﴿We have decreed﴾. And since the verb of decreeing includes knowledge, He suspended it from His saying: ﴿that she﴾; that is, his wife; and He emphasized it because of what is indicated here of the great eagerness of the Friend (peace be upon him) to know their affair, and the intensity of his question concerning the salvation of Lot (peace be upon him) and all his family, as has already been stated explicitly in "Hud"; so as to wean him from asking about her salvation. This differs from what is in "An-Naml", for its context is free of that. ﴿Surely she is of those who remain behind﴾; that is, those who remain, who will not be saved along with Lot (peace be upon him), but will be in the destruction and as a lesson.

"Al-Al" (the family): al-Rummani said: the people of one whose authority they return to; for this reason one says "ahl al-balad" (the people of the land) and does not say "al al-balad". The principle is: "a thing is set at the measure of another, so that equality and difference may appear." And "al-ghabir" (those who remain): the one who remains among those who perish.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 61:

When the report about their dialogue with Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was complete, he reported their matter with Lut (peace be upon him). So He said: ﴿Then when﴾ with the fa' (fa, "then"), which indicates the speed of their arrival to him. It is as if his denial of them only intensified after they had entered his dwelling, either out of his fear for them, while they were not afraid, or due to other circumstances that do not resemble the circumstances of humans. Therefore He said: ﴿the messengers came to the family of Lut﴾, meaning: into his dwelling; ﴿the messengers﴾, meaning: sent for the destruction of his people.

He said, "Indeed, you are a people unknown [to me]." That is, (ﷺ) ... 

Let me restate precisely: He said, "Indeed, you are a people [who are] strangers" — that is, [people] whom he does not know; and that is the meaning of "He was distressed on their account" [Hud: 77], the verse etc. So he mentioned his denial of them first and their informing him of the punishment, in the same manner as what preceded in the story of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), by way of rebuking them for their saying: "Why do you not bring us the angels?" [al-Hijr: 7], which may refer to all the angels, "if you are among the truthful" [al-Hijr: 7]. This is to make them aware that some of the angels came to the two most perfect people of that time, in the most beautiful forms of humans, bringing good news to them, and yet each of them was frightened. So how would it be if there were a great multitude of them? Or how would it be if they were in their own forms? Or how would it be if the one who saw them were someone other than those two? Or how would it be if he were a disbeliever? "On the day they see the angels, there will be no good news that day for the criminals, and they will say, 'A forbidding ban!'" [al-Furqan: 22].

It is also possible that his saying this statement to them was only when they informed him that they were messengers of Allah; and the meaning then would be: "Indeed, you are not in the description of those who come with revelation; your affair has become severe upon me, since I do not know you," together with the uneasiness I feel from you; and that was after his dialogue with his people and then his contention with them on their behalf, so he was anxious for them. When they told him that they were angels, he feared from them that they had come with something he would dislike. It has already been mentioned earlier that reporting what occurred at some time does not harm the placing of some of it before another, nor the omission of some, and the mention of another; and here he did not add the particle that originally is the verbal noun, which is "an" (أنْ), as in al-'Ankabut, because his denunciation of them, although it is consequent upon their coming, is not connected to its beginning, unlike the distress.

Since the reality of the unfamiliar (munkar) is that which departs from the custom of its kind and does not follow the manner of its like, they turned away from his saying, and their answer was that they said, "Rather," ﴿Rather we have come to you﴾; that is, we are not unfamiliar with it, because we have come to you ﴿to deliver you﴾ from it, ﴿with that﴾; that is, by reason of bringing about what ﴿they used to﴾; that is, by natural disposition and inclination, ﴿doubt concerning﴾; with what our custom has been to bring the like of from the punishment, which they used to doubt greatly, bearing their souls toward it and denying it. The ignorant person is described as one who doubts, even if he is a denier, because of what occurs to him from it, in that he does not return to any certainty regarding what he is upon;

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 64:

﴿And We have brought you the truth﴾; the decisive one that distinguishes between you and them; the one that befalls them in conformity with Our report. And "al-ityan" (coming to): moving toward the direction of a thing; and "al-dhahab" (going): moving away from it; (p-72) ﴿And indeed We are truthful﴾; in reporting that which corresponds to reality.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 65:

When they informed him that the punishment had befallen them, they commanded him with what would be the means of fulfilling what they had been commanded regarding his deliverance. So they said: ﴿So travel by night﴾. They used the particle *fa* (so), because what follows it is a consequence of what precedes it. ﴿with your family in a portion﴾, that is, a part of ﴿the night﴾. ﴿And follow﴾, that is, exert yourself to follow ﴿their rear﴾ (*dubur*, the back or rear side, the opposite of *qubul*, the front), so that you may be the nearest of them to us and to the place of punishment, because you are the steadiest of them in heart and the most knowing of them of God. ﴿And the evil is behind you.﴾ It has been the custom of leaders that they position themselves nearest to the frightening matter among their group, out of generosity with their own selves, to steady others, and in knowledge that drawing near to what causes fear does not bring a closer term of life, and its opposite does not avert decree, nor does it keep away harm. Also, so that your heart will not be occupied with those who opposed you, and so that they will feel ashamed before you and not look back, or so that none of them will lag behind; and other benefits. ﴿Let none of you look back﴾, that is, at all, ﴿for there is no benefit in it﴾, since the one who looks back is not steadfast, for he is either not certain of our report or grieves for them; whoever looks back will be struck by the punishment. This is also more effective in the migration and swifter in the journey, and more indicative of removing from their hearts what they left behind of their dwellings and belongings, and of their not being softened toward those upon whom God is angry, even though they may see what their souls cannot bear. ﴿And proceed to where you are commanded.﴾ His expression in the present tense indicates that some of the angels (peace be upon them) will be with them, in His saying: ﴿you are commanded﴾.

And We decreed that matter to him, that the last of these people would be cut off at dawn, (ﷺ)... 

Let me translate it properly:

When this matter had been established, the matter of their destruction without explicit statement or specification of a time, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We decreed﴾; that is, by the majesty We possess; revealing ﴿to him﴾; that is, specifically; ﴿that matter﴾; and He indicated its magnitude by pointing to it with the demonstrative of distance; then He explained it with His saying: ﴿that the last remnant of﴾; that is, the last; ﴿these﴾; that is, those who are insignificant in the face of Our power; and He indicated, by the form of the passive participle, His greatness — glory be to Him — and the ease of the matter with Him; so Allah the Exalted said: ﴿would be cut off﴾; while they were ﴿at dawn﴾.

The "dābir" (remnant, last of a people) is not cut off until whatever is before it is cut off, because the enemy confronts its enemy in order; so it is a metaphor for complete eradication, that their last and first are equal in being seized, because the One seizing them is capable — not as some people do with one another, who grow weary at the end of battles, so that some of them escape.

Then, when what had passed between him and the messengers was complete, introducing what would be explained, he followed it with an account of the state of his people, as an indication that the angels, if they were in human attributes, the disbelievers would not recognize them; and if they were in their own attributes, or displaying something of their extraordinary powers, their strength would not bear it, so there would be no benefit for them in seeing them face to face in any state whatsoever. Their demand that they bring them (the angels) was therefore great ignorance. So He (Exalted) said: ﴿And the people of the city came﴾; that is, the city in which this matter was (they said: it is Sodom), out of desire to commit the abomination with the guests; ﴿rejoicing﴾; that is, joy shows upon their faces, so they produce it for themselves as one who is most eager in seeking it.

Thus the state of Lut, peace be upon him, was that he said to them: "Indeed these are my guests" — that is, those who are close to me — "so do not disgrace me." Since honouring a guest is an honouring of the one whose guest he is, and insulting him is an insult to that host, he drew from this the consequence that the speech had indicated, and said: "So do not disgrace me [by inflicting upon them an immoral act]." And this was before he knew that they were angels.
"Fear Allah"; that is, the One to whom belongs all greatness. "And do not disgrace me"; that is, by humiliating my guests, for that would be a shame upon me for all time.

Then that did not satisfy them; rather they said (﴿qālū﴾), harshly, conjoining to what its implied sense is: "Do you not know that we do not abandon this matter for any reason at all?": ﴿Did we not forbid you from the people of the worlds?﴾; that is, from before this; ﴿from the people of the worlds﴾; that you should not give protection (tujīr) against us to any of them;

When they had reached this degree of shamelessness, he mentioned to them the women (of his household), so that this would move them to modesty, for that is the custom of one who has even a little manliness (muruwwa), especially the mention of the virgins, in a context that almost states his intent plainly. So he said, ﴿These are my daughters, if you are going to act﴾, indicating his house in which his daughters were, may peace and blessings be upon him and may Allah be pleased with them; ﴿if you are to do it﴾, that is, you have resolved firmly upon this act. The use of the particle of doubt (in "if") indicates that this act is one that should not be done, meaning: and you know that I will never surrender my daughters. From this it is known that your reaching my guests without destroying me is impossible.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 72:

When He had mentioned what He mentioned of their affairs and the enormity of their wickedness, and their affair had already been concluded and their destruction decreed, anyone who knew this would judge that they have no intellects. So, glory be to Him, He followed this with what indicates it, saying: ﴿By your life﴾; that is, by your life, O you of noble character. He emphasized it because the situation at that time called for the improbability of their turning back, and to establish that this was pure misguidance on their part and sheer obstinacy: so He said, ﴿Indeed, they are in their intoxication﴾; that is, in their jahili (pre-Islamic ignorant) error; ﴿wandering blindly﴾; that is, bewildered, not seeing the path of right guidance. Therefore they do not accept the counsel of the sincere advisor. If the one addressed is Lut (peace be upon him), the pronoun of the third person refers to his people. If the one addressed is our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and this is the apparent meaning, the pronoun refers to his people, and the sense is that they are in a deep confusion, far from the ways (sunan), in their seeking to have intercourse with the angels, just as the people of Lut (peace be upon him) intended to gratify themselves with the foul act, with those whom they were empowered to destroy. How far apart are the two intentions! And how distant are the two acts from each other! The meaning becomes that what they accused you of at the beginning of the surah belongs to them, not to you, because whoever seeks to have intercourse with the angels, even though his condition may be like that of the people of Lut (peace be upon him) when they had intercourse, is the one who is mad.

Regarding al-ʿamr (ﭐ), with a fatha: ﭐ, meaning "life," and with a damma: ﭐ, meaning "lifespan," which is the duration of a thing's remaining alive. But in an oath it is only said with a fatha, because of its lightness, given the frequent occurrence of oaths. For this reason they omitted the word whose implied form would be "my oath." Al-sakrah is the overwhelming of the self by heedlessness.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 73:

When that was complete, he (the author) connected the decree to cut off their last remnant with His (Exalted be He) saying: ﴿So the Shout seized them﴾; that is, a seizing of vengeance and overpowering; ﴿the Shout﴾; that is, the one which, because of its magnitude and terror, is the Shout, and anything else is nothing in comparison to it. And al-akhdh (seizing) is an action by which a thing comes into the direction of the agent; and al-sayha (the shout) is a sound that comes out of the mouth with force. His saying: ﴿at sunrise﴾ means entering into al-ishraq (sunrise), which is the light of the sun (p-77) at its rising. And it becomes clear from this that their time is called subh (morning) linguistically, for al-subh, al-sabah and al-isbah are the beginning of the day. Perhaps it is applied to it until the time of the morning meal, or until midday. Or the Shout occurred at the time of sunrise as the last of their affair, and the uprooting of the cities from their places at the time of morning was the beginning of their affair.

Then He, glory be to Him, explained what resulted from the Cry, following it closely, and said: ﴿So We made its highest part its lowest﴾; that is, their cities. ﴿And We rained upon them﴾. Since the rebuke in this surah was greater than the rebuke in Surah Hud (upon him be peace), because they asked that all the angels be brought, He returned the pronoun to the people who were punished, not to their cities, as had passed in Surah Hud (upon him be peace), because this is more explicit. So He said: ﴿upon them﴾; that is, the people of the cities whose cities were overturned on their account, ﴿stones of baked clay﴾.

Then he verified that all of that is an explanation of His words: ﴿And that those of understanding may take heed﴾ [Ibrahim: 52]; by His words: ﴿Indeed in that﴾; that is, the matter, which is very great; ﴿are signs﴾; that is, many; in terms of its being submerged in water after its sinking; and in terms of its being contrary to the waters of the earth in its foulness and corruption; and the absence of animal life in it; and the absence of benefit from it; and in terms of the hideousness of its appearance; and other aspects of its condition; ﴿for those who discern﴾; the plural of "mutawassim" (one who discerns, one who reads signs); this is the one who looks into the distinguishing mark (simah), which is the indicative trace on the face and the circumstantial indications that point to good and evil. (p-78) They used to claim that they were the most perceptive of people in such matters; so this is a spur to them and a rebuke.

Then he showed that this is not hidden from them, nor far from anyone who wishes to take admonition from it. So he said, placing them in the ranks of the deniers, since they do not take heed from it despite seeing it at all times: ﴿And indeed they are on a road that remains﴾; that is, these towns; ﴿on a road that remains﴾; that is, established. Yet it is clear (mubin) despite this; so taking heed from it is extremely easy for your people, and they used to pass by it on some of their journeys to Syria.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 77:

When He (glory be to Him) pointed to the inference by means of the tawassum (discerning sign, firasa), which indicates, through the way in which this place differs from all the other sweet waters of the earth that flow into it in abundance, and although the lands in which it lies are among the most delightful lands in the sweetness of their waters, the freshness of their soil, the beauty of their trees and other things, and that it has a report which is most strange, and He followed that with the ease of reaching it, as an incitement to come to it with the intention of looking at it, taking lessons from it, and asking about the cause of its being thus, He said, pointing to the increase of exhortation through emphasis: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign﴾; that is, in this great matter of its condition; ﴿a sign﴾; that is, a great indication pointing us to Him; ﴿for the believers﴾; that is, those firmly established in truthfulness and in affirmation. For when they are told that the cause of its being thus is that Allah commanded some of His soldiers, so they lifted it up, then overturned it, then pursued it with stones, then caused the earth to swallow it, and submerged it (p-٧٩) with this water, which is in its foulness and lack of fruitfulness suited to the deeds of its people, because of their disobedience to His Messenger (ﷺ), they believed, out of fear of a punishment like this, believing in the unseen.

When he had mentioned this story, he appended to it what is of the same kind, of the punishment with which he afflicted his people by another type of punishment, resembling the punishment of the people of Lot in that it was fire from the sky. So he said, emphasizing (ta'kid) to remove the disbelievers' denial that their punishment was on account of denying [the messenger], or counting them (ʿadd) — because of their persistence in error despite knowing it — among the deniers: ﴿And indeed﴾; i.e., verily it; ﴿was﴾; i.e., by nature and disposition; ﴿the companions of the Thicket﴾; and they are the people of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him; and "al-Aykah" (the thicket): the tree, according to al-Hasan; its plural is "al-Ayk," like "shajarah" and "shajar"; and it has been said: "al-Aykah" is densely intertwined trees; ﴿were indeed wrongdoers﴾; i.e., those who were extreme (al-'arīqīn) in wrongdoing.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 79:

﴿So We took vengeance upon them﴾; i.e., because of that. Then He informed about the two towns, because they were close to each other in punishment, in place, and in being on one of the roads of the trade routes of Quraysh. So He said: ﴿And indeed, they both﴾; i.e., the villages of the people of Lot and the dwelling places of the companions of al-Aykah; ﴿are on a highway [imam]﴾; i.e., a road that is followed, taken as a path, and by which one is guided; ﴿clear﴾; evident to whoever seeks it. In such a way that, from the intensity of its clarity, it makes clear the greatness of Allah (p-80) and His support of His prophets against those who deny them. And it, despite its clarity, remains in its place; its landmarks have not been effaced and its traces have not been obliterated. So the verse is of the type of ihtibak (interlocking omission): He mentioned in the first "muqim" (remaining), indicating the omission of its like in the second; and in the second "mubin" (clear), indicating the omission of its like in the first.

Since it might be said, "If the People of the Thicket had sturdy houses, these would have protected them from the punishment," He followed them with those who were on another route, [namely] their trade routes to the Levant. They had long been deluded by hope, to the point that they took the mountains as houses, and their sign was of the utmost clarity, yet they denied it. This is to establish that the obstinate, if they saw every sign, would say, "Our eyes have only been dazzled." So He said: ﴿And indeed the companions of the Rock denied the messengers﴾. And since the context concerns those who denied and what befell them through their denial, He placed the agent first, and said, indicating the soundness of their houses: ﴿the companions of the Rock﴾. They are Thamud, the people of Salih (peace be upon him), whose dwellings lay between the Noble City and the Levant. ﴿The messengers﴾, meaning all of them, by denying their messenger, just as these [people] denied you, [O Muhammad], since the messengers bear witness to one another's truthfulness. Whoever denies one of them has denied all of them, and they are equal in establishing prophethood through miracles.

Then he followed this with His saying: ﴿And We gave them﴾; that is, by Our majesty; through their messenger Salih, peace be upon him (p-81) ﴿Our signs﴾; that is, all of them; by bringing the she-camel, and her watering, her milk, and her drinking. For all possible things are equal in relation to His power; so whoever denies one of them has denied all of them. ﴿Yet they turned away﴾; that is, in a state of constant disposition, like a natural nature; ﴿from them﴾; that is, from the signs, all of them, specifically; not from the adornment of the world which drags one to falsehood; ﴿turning away﴾; that is, firmly persisting in aversion; they did not believe in them. This is in reference to His saying (exalted is He): ﴿And even if We opened for them a gate from the heaven﴾ [al-Hijr: 14], the two verses; and as an illustration of it; a returning of the conclusion to the opening (radd al-maqta' 'ala al-matla').

Then He informed that they were like these (people) in their security from the punishment, and in their heedlessness of what was intended for them, even though they were stronger than them. So He said: ﴿And they used to hew out (dwellings) from the mountains﴾. And "an-nahtu" (hewing): removing part after part from a body, by way of scraping, ﴿from the mountains﴾, which it has already been mentioned that We made as firm anchors (rawasi). ﴿Houses, secure﴾, safe from collapse upon them, and from the reaching of what is disliked by them; unlike your houses, which have no permanence whatsoever.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 83:

﴿So the Blast seized them﴾; that is, as a consequence of their denial, the Blast seized them with the seizing of punishment and retribution, ﴿while they were entering upon the morning﴾; that is, they were in the time of dawn.

So the cry (al-sayha) brought about that what they used to earn did not avail them at all. ﴿Fa-ma aghna 'anhum ma kanu yaksibun﴾: "so what they used to earn did not avail them" — that is, did not suffice them, with respect to their natural dispositions, from houses, works, equipment, and wicked instruments. For nothing can defeat Us, since there is no difficulty for Us in what We do: We only say to it "Be," and it is. We did this to them because they were upon falsehood, so Our punishment of them was just.

Since the one who seeks to trip up might say: "Why would He create them and then destroy them, when He, at the time He created them, knew that they would deny?" And this verse, along with its mention of the earth, was turning back toward that earlier verse, which was followed by the mention of the two horizons, as evidence for the Hour. He said, following that same pattern: ﴿And We did not create the heavens﴾, i.e., with Our greatness; ﴿and the earth﴾, with its benefits and wonders; ﴿and what is between them﴾, of these deniers and their punishment; and of waters, winds, and clouds, from which plants are caused, and other things; ﴿except with truth﴾, i.e., creation intertwined with truth, so that whoever Allah grants success reflects upon it and thereby knows the final creation from this first creation. Or it means by means of the truth of establishing fixed matters and negating what would shake them, so that Our greatness may appear by granting the oppressed justice against the oppressor, rewarding the obedient, and punishing the disobedient on the Day of Judgment, along with other wisdoms. As He (Exalted) said: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, that He may recompense those who did evil with what they did and recompense those who did good with the best﴾ [al-Najm: 31]. So whoever We give respite in this world, We will take from him his right after the Hour is established; so it must be done. ﴿And indeed the Hour is coming﴾, for the sake of establishing the truth; there is no doubt in its coming, by the judgment of His knowledge, glorified is He, so all of that will appear in it. It is also possible that the implied meaning is: "So what they used to earn did not avail them. We did not do that except by the command of Our saying 'Be,' and it is the truth." "We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth," i.e., by the command. "Surely to Him belong creation and command." This means that there is no hardship for Us in any of that, and We will bring it to nothing with truth when We want the Hour to be established. ﴿And indeed the Hour is coming﴾, because We have promised that, and between you and its existence there is nothing but that We will, so it is, as was the case with others that We willed. ﴿So forgive with gracious forgiveness﴾, i.e., turn away, because the taking of your revenge is certain, with a fine turning away, ﴿gracious﴾, with forbearance, overlooking, and breadth of chest, like their saying: ﴿O you to whom the Reminder has been sent, indeed you are mad﴾ [al-Hijr: 6]. For there is no escaping that We will take from them on your behalf with truth, and even if you had no victory except on that day, it would be sufficient for you.

Then He gave the reason for this command by saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord﴾, that is, the One who does good to you and who commands you in this. ﴿He﴾ (p-84), that is, alone, ﴿is the Creator (al-Khallaq)﴾, the One who repeatedly performs this act at every moment merely by the command. So there is nothing strange in His bringing into existence what is attributed to Him of originating the Hour or other than it. He is also, for that reason, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of all your conditions, and of what among them is good for you, in perfect wisdom. For the one who forms a picture knows it better than the one who looks at it and considers it, the maker of a thing knows it better than its buyer, and the builder of a house knows it better than its occupant. He is the One who created all that you see of them, so it is His doing, so submit to Him.

Since the perfecting of created things cannot be complete except through knowledge, He (may He be exalted) said: ﴿the All-Knowing (al-Alim)﴾, that is, the one whose knowledge of all knowable things is complete. So you do not see their deeds and their words except from Him, glory be to Him, because He is their Creator. You know that He does not lose even the weight of an atom's worth, so rely upon Him in taking your right, for He is an excellent Protector and an excellent Helper, and nothing from it is hidden from Him. What I have said is confirmed by the verse of Ya Sin: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? Yes, and He is the Creator, the All-Knowing﴾ [Ya Sin: 81]. Or it may be said: ﴿what they used to earn did not avail them at all﴾ of the truth that We intended, because We did not create their punishment except with truth, just as We created them with truth, so nothing of that was impossible for Us. ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾ [al-Hijr: 85], that is, for the sake of establishing the truth and manifesting Our command in justice. Had We not empowered some people over others, this attribute of Ours would not have appeared to them in its fullest manifestation. So We hasten, from the truth for the sake of which We created that, up to the establishment of the Hour, whatever We will of trial and retribution, as We did with those whose matters We have narrated, and We defer of that what remains until the establishment of the Hour. ﴿Indeed, the Hour is coming﴾ [al-Hijr: 85], there is no doubt about it, so We will leave nothing of rights there unfulfilled. ﴿So forgive with gracious forgiveness﴾ [al-Hijr: 85]. There must be a taking of your right, either in this world or in the Hereafter. ﴿Indeed﴾, that is, because ﴿your Lord is the Creator﴾, that is, the One who performs creation again and again, whose power is never exhausted and whose word is never diminished, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾, the one of perfect knowledge. So He is capable of that, and knows the wisdom in it, in its time and in its manner. He will restore the creatures on the Hour as He originated them, and will then fulfill all rights, and He will grant you on that Day what will comfort your eye.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 87:

When He mentioned the attribute of knowledge in the intensive form (ṣīghat al-mubālagha), He followed it with what He had bestowed in this world of the material of knowledge, in the form of majesty (ṣīghat al-ʿaẓama). So He said, coordinating (ʿaṭfan) with what I have estimated (qaddartuhu), which the context indicates: ﴿And We have certainly given you﴾, which indicates Our knowledge; ﴿seven of the oft-repeated﴾, and they are al-Fatiha, which comprises, despite its brevity, all the meanings of the Qur'an; it is repeated (tuthannā) in revelation, for it was revealed twice; and it is repeated (tuthannā) in every rak'a of the prayer; and it is praise of Allah and of His righteous servants; and it is divided between Allah and His servant; and its purposes are repeated (tuthannā) within it, and each of its meanings is presented in it by different methods in clarifying the indication of it, in the molds of words and the essential structures of composition that guide to it, and other than that of repetition; ﴿and the Great Qur'an﴾, that is, the one that contains all the sciences of the first and the last ones, of what is in all the earlier books and other than them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 88:

Since what He had given him, and what He would yet give him, is greater than anything given to any creature, there followed His words: ﴿Do not strain your eyes﴾; that is, with a great straining, through wishing and fixed desire; and for this reason He mentioned the eyes (dual) to exclude the inner talk of the soul; ﴿toward what We have provided﴾; that is, despite Our greatness; ﴿to pairs of them﴾; that is, kinds; ﴿of them﴾; that is, the people of the world. Or it may be said: since the aim for every person of understanding is only the conveying from the abode of perishing to the abode of permanence, whose coming is emphasized in the preceding verse, and since the Qur'an, as has passed, was sufficient for that and consoled him, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, concerning what they harm him with of their words, and it became clear from this the loftiness of his rank, the listener anticipated mention of what (p-87) He had lavished upon him of blessings. So He, (exalted), said, or it may be said: since He, glorified is He, had commanded him to be patient over their harm, He gave the reason for that with a meaning to the effect that they are His creation, that He alone creates, that He has perfect knowledge of their deeds, that He wills them, so the act in reality belongs to none but Him; and the lover should be content with the deed of his beloved insofar as it is his deed. Since the implied sense was: "He is the One who created them, and knew before their creation what they would do," He followed it, as consolation for him, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, with His words: ﴿And We have certainly given you﴾ [al-Hijr: 87]; that is, with what We possess of greatness; as We gave Salih what has passed; ﴿seven of the oft-repeated﴾ [al-Hijr: 87]; each seven of them being sufficient to close one of the seven gates of the Fires; and they are Umm al-Qur'an (the Mother of the Qur'an), comprehensive of all the meanings of the Qur'an, which we were commanded to repeat in every rak'ah, for increase in its preservation, for blessing through its wording, and for remembrance of its meanings, singling it out from the rest of the remembrance which We have undertaken to preserve; ﴿and⦆; We gave you ﴿the great Qur'an﴾; comprehensive of all the meanings of the heavenly books, undertaking the good of both abodes, together with countless additions; its greatness was indicated at the beginning of the surah by the tanwin, and it is described as clarifying the manifest proofs of your prophethood and the decisive evidences of your messengership, indicating Allah and leading to Him. The verse, moreover, is evidence for the knowledge with which the preceding verses were concluded. So it is as if it were said: "Then what shall I do?" (p-88) It was said, in the sense of "Leave them to eat": ﴿Do not strain your eyes toward what We have provided to pairs of them﴾, being content with this great message, which whoever adorns himself with and whose heart is saturated with it, Allah shows him the defects of this abode, so he dislikes it, and it lets him overlook what lies ahead; ﴿and do not grieve over them﴾, for their not believing, so that they might save their souls from the Fire, and the side of Islam might be strengthened through them; and this seems to be the forgiving pardon commanded, which is turning away from them entirely, except in the matter of conveying the message.

Since He commanded him regarding their company with what He commanded, He followed it with His command regarding the companionship of his Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, with gentleness and softness, so He, (exalted), said: ﴿And lower your wing﴾; that is, humble yourself; ﴿to the believers﴾; that is, those who are steadfast in this description; and restrain yourself with them, and be content with them, for Allah will place blessing among them, and be your helper, and the strengthener of your religion through them, and He will not make you need others; so whoever desires their wretchedness, do not turn toward them. This is a metaphor for gentleness, and its origin is that when a bird gathers its chick to itself, it spreads its wing, then folds it over the chick; so said Abu Hayyan. And in the tenth part of al-Thaqafiyyat, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "The believer is gentle, until you think him foolish out of gentleness."

And since the prevailing trait of human nature is shortcoming, He said to him: ﴿And say﴾; that is, to both groups, emphasizing for the disbelievers their denial and for the believers the contentment of soul that is theirs through it: ﴿Indeed, I am﴾; that is, not anyone other than me among the warners against worldly enemies, ﴿the clear warner﴾; for whoever deliberately falls short, my warning rescues him from his peril, because it is surrounded by decisive proofs.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 90:

When he had mentioned what was joined to the story of the companions of al-Hijr, who divided themselves (al-muqtasimin) against killing their messenger, and concluded it with the warning to which they belong, he returned to completing their matter. He likened them to those of this community who denied, and so said: ﴿As﴾; that is, those [earlier ones] denied, and We gave them Our signs, but they turned away from them; so We inflicted upon them of the punishment that they deserved; ﴿just as﴾ We ﴿sent down﴾; that is, by Our majesty, of the signs; ﴿upon the dividers﴾; that is, the likes of them; from Quraysh, when they divided the mountain passes of Makkah, driving people away from you and scattering their speech about the Qur'an. So do not grieve over them for their denial and their obstinacy, despite seeing the clear signs; for Our way (sunnah) has proceeded thus concerning whomever We intend to be wretched, such as the people of Salih;

Then He said: ﴿Those﴾; that is, even though they conspired against you and divided the roads of Makkah to turn people away from you; ﴿who have made the Qur'an﴾; by their statements; ﴿into fragments﴾; that is, they divided their speech about it, while in fact it is (p-90) a gatherer of meanings, not a scatterer of wording; most firmly ordered in its composition, most harmoniously interconnected in its coherence; as we have already pointed out by naming it a Book and a Qur'an, and we concluded that this is in the manner of clear exposition, with no obscurity in it. So their speech is entirely obstinacy: they said "sorcery," they said "poetry," they said "soothsaying," they said "fables of the ancients," and other things. We sent down to them Our clear signs and Our manifest proofs, but they turned away from them and occupied themselves with what does not benefit them, such as obstinate fault-finding and other things, following the practice of those (earlier people); so let them await the like of what befell them. And like them is everyone who speaks about the Qur'an in such a way, of the Arabs and others, in a manner that is not fitting. Al-Bukhari narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father: ﴿They have made the Qur'an into fragments﴾; he said: They are the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians; they divided it into parts, so they believed in some of it and disbelieved in some of it. The meaning of this word will come later.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 92:

﴿Then by your Lord﴾; i.e., as a consequence of their action, We swear by the One who brought you into being, who manages your affair, who has done good to you by sending you; ﴿We will surely question them all﴾; i.e., these and those.

﴿Concerning what they used to do﴾; i.e., a state of conduct that was their innate disposition; ﴿they were doing﴾; i.e., of dividing the Qur'an into parts (ta'diyah) and other things; because We shall question every one of them about what he did.

(p-٩١) Meaning: proclaim openly, with force and firmness, separating truth from falsehood by means of that which you are commanded to convey, namely the Qur'an and "a clear Book." ﴿And turn away﴾, that is, turn away as one who is indifferent, ﴿from the polytheists﴾, by forgiving their harm graciously and striving in the call (to Islam). That "as" (in His words "as") refers back to the story of Salih and is connected to it, although I have not seen anyone who preceded me in saying so, is supported by the mention of the attribute through which the two verses are linked, which is the act of dividing (the Qur'an among themselves). Then comes the description of those who divided it as "those who made the Qur'an into parts" (ʿidin), lest it be assumed that they are the ones who conspired at night against Salih. That is: We gave those (people of Thamud) the signs that call for faith, but they responded only with denial and conspiracy, just as We sent down these signs upon these (Quraysh), and they responded with nothing but that. The verb used for those (people) is "We gave them" (ātaynāhum), because their signs were the she-camel, her offspring, and the well, which were given and are tangible, not sent down as abstract revelation. For these (Quraysh) the verb is "We sent down" (anzalnā), indicating the Qur'an, which is the greatest of signs, or indicating all of them, and the Qur'an is given precedence over them because it is the greatest of them, and because they are wrongdoers in their denial, and it is not fitting for them to entertain any doubt that it is sent down, since it is greater than those signs, even though those were tangible. As for the insertion of the verses between these two (the story and the command), it is among the greatest refinements of eloquence (balagha). When He had completed the story of Salih, peace be upon him, He knew that the obstinate might say: "Why does He create them and then destroy them, knowing that they will not respond?" So He answered them by saying that He did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them, including these stubborn deniers, their deeds, their punishment, and other things, except with truth, and that the Hour is surely coming. Then all of that will be known by sight to those who now doubt it, on the day when the veil is lifted from insights and sights. ﴿So forgive them﴾, for there must be a taking of your right, if not in this world then on the Day of Gathering. Then He confirmed the disposition with wisdom by His words: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is the Creator, the All-Knowing﴾. Then He consoled him regarding what they press upon his chest by way of denial of the Hour, and their claim that the promise of it is mere sorcery, and similar speech, and their boasting of their wealth, and their attribution to him of a need to walk in the markets, by what He had given him of the treasures of the Qur'an. He commanded him to increase in humility and gentleness toward the believers, so that their souls might be content and they would not grieve over what of worldly things escaped them, and to warn all people and caution them against the punishments of God, like those that befell the earlier peoples. Then He returned to them and likened them to those (earlier peoples) in denial, so that it would be known that they are more deserving of punishment than those, because they are the ones being likened, and what is likened to is higher than what it is likened to. That is because they are more intense in disbelief, since their Prophet is greater, his signs are more majestic and more numerous, and clearer and more dazzling, so that this would be the cause of intensifying their caution. You may also say, and this is perhaps the better view: when He (exalted is He) mentioned that Thamud dwelt in the land in the security of those at ease, then a Cry (ṣayḥa) overtook them and removed them from it, a Cry that took their spirits and turned their bodies over, just as there will be for all the people of the earth a blast of the Trumpet, when the decree is carried out. He had earlier mentioned much of what is in the heavens and the earth of signs and lessons, by His words (exalted is He): ﴿And We have placed in the sky constellations﴾, and what follows of jinn, humans and others, which made the mention of their origination a proof of the Hour. He then followed that with the fact that the reason for creating all of that and what it contains of the two regions (the heavens and the earth) is only the Hour. So He said: ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾, that is, by a firmly established matter, not by deception and sorcery, as you witness. Or (it means) by the cause of establishing the truth and distinguishing it from falsehood, a distinction in which there is no doubt, on the Great Day of Gathering. Among the establishment of truth is the bliss of the obedient and the punishment of the disobedient, and that is after the coming of the Hour with the two blasts of the Trumpet. And indeed the Hour is surely coming in truth as well, and it is not sorcery as you suppose. Since its coming for this purpose is what soothes the heart, by attaining retribution, and that is a truth that must come, His words (exalted is He) follow as a consequence: ﴿So forgive with gracious forgiveness﴾. (p-٩٤) Since the soul is more firmly assured by the report of the One who knows best, and the maker of a thing knows it better than anyone else, how much more so when He also has perfect knowledge? God (exalted is He) said, giving the reason for this: ﴿Indeed, your Lord﴾, that is, the One who does good to you, ﴿is the Creator﴾, that is, the one of complete power to originate and to annihilate, the doer of that, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾, the one whose knowledge is complete. And when He concluded with these two attributes, after having mentioned what the people of al-Hijr were given of signs, and that He created existence by truth and not by deception, and since this made it expected that He would inform about what this noble Prophet was given of them, for the guidance of his community, and since the signs are either of the category of creation, like the sign of Salih, or of the category of command, which is the basis of knowledge, He pointed to the preference of him (ﷺ) through the excellence of his sign. So He said, linking this to what precedes: ﴿And We have certainly given you﴾, that is: if We gave Salih or others a sign that has passed and only its mention remains, then We have given you seven of the oft-repeated (al-mathani), which is al-Fatihah, the opening chapter, by which you were singled out. In it the basmala is repeated for beginnings, the hamdala for perfections, and the "Most Merciful" and "Most Compassionate" (in it) for the first origination; and for what is pleasing of deeds; and the kingship of this world, called lordship (rubūbiyya), because it is hidden; and the kingship of the Day of Judgment; and between them the "Most Merciful" quality of the second origination, which is the return, and the "Most Compassionate" quality of reward for the pleasing causes; (p-٩٥) and the worship that is only possible with power and choice; and the seeking of help, which looks to one's inability to attain full power; and guidance through the Guide and the one guided; and error, in contrast to that, through the one who misleads and the one who is misled. In this are secrets that thoughts cannot contain. And the noble Qur'an, which comprises all signs, while being a firmly established truth, not sorcery or illusion, but a sign that remains throughout time, whose matter is ongoing and whose recitation and remembrance are perpetual. The firm mountains will pass away while it remains, and the heavens and the earths will vanish while it is still fresh. When the ranks of the wicked line up, every verse of it will say: "Is there any challenger?" And if an enemy seeks to prolong the contest, thinking it weak, it will cry out, by the enduring of its strength: "I am ready to engage!" No one stands against it, none circles around its sanctuary, and none desires to plunge into its sea. Since this verse is sufficient for its bearer, and pleasing and satisfying to whoever has been granted its acceptance, it was altogether fitting to follow it with His words: ﴿Do not extend your eyes toward what We have given enjoyment to some pairs of them with﴾, and since their disbelief after its clarification is only obstinacy, He said: ﴿And do not grieve over them﴾. And since the wealthy one by it might suppose the nobility of pride in wealth, He followed it with: ﴿And lower your wing to the believers﴾. And since he might suppose that its recitation makes supplication unnecessary, especially for one who turns away, He negated that by His words: ﴿And say: "I am only a clear warner"﴾, as an incitement to striving in warning, a strengthening of the believers, a humbling of the obstinate, and an attraction of those among the disbelievers whom God wills to make happy, informing that hearts of believers are in the hand of God, exalted and glorified is He, so there is no trust in one who comes forward, nor safety from one who turns away.

When all of this was complete in this firm arrangement and this strong, tight connection, the mind turned to the state of those he warns. The disbelievers of Quraysh, in their dividing of speech about the Qur'an and their parceling out of the paths of Makkah to spread that slander in order to repel whoever wished to believe, were most like those who divided against Salih, peace be upon him. God (exalted is He) said: ﴿As﴾, that is: We gave those dividers Our signs, and they turned away from them, ﴿just as We sent down Our signs upon the dividers﴾, that is, those who divided with great eagerness and striving in that, ﴿who made the Qur'an into parts﴾, that is, having members, meaning separate, distinct pieces, like the limbs of a slaughtered camel when cut up, the plural of ʿidha, like ʿidda, and its original form is ʿidwa. ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾, that is, none of them can escape Us, ﴿about what they used to do.﴾ ﴿So proclaim openly what you are commanded﴾, that is: because of Our command to you to warn, and your being informed that We will question each one about what he did. ﴿And turn away from the polytheists.﴾

(p-97) Since this breaking-off (ṣadʿ) was extremely hard upon him, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, because of the abundance of harm he suffered, He—glory be to Him—lightened it for him by His saying, giving the reason for it: ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you﴾; that is, with what We possess of greatness; ﴿against the mockers﴾; that is, the worst of those who are deeply immersed in mocking you and what you have brought. So We comforted your eye by their destruction, the burden of what they inflicted upon you was lifted from you, and its reward remains for you. And We shall suffice you against others besides them, just as We sufficed you against them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 96:

Then He described them by His saying: ﴿Those who set up another god along with Allah⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿—⁠﻿⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿—⁠ that is, alongside what they saw of His signs, which indicate His majesty, the greatness of His encompassing power, and His perfection⁠﻿⁠﻿﻿﻿—⁠ ﴾⁠﻿﻿⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿—⁠ ﴿a god﴾. Since being "with" (al-ma'iyyah) conveys otherness (al-ghayriyyah), especially when expressed with the verb "to make" (al-ja'l), and since some obstinate person among them might have tried to exploit the possibility that the threat was directed at His being called God in an unqualified way, or at His being invoked by a name other than the Majestic Name (al-Jalalah), in light of what the exegetes mentioned regarding His saying: ﴿Say: Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful⁠﻿⁠﻿﻿﻿—⁠﻿⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿—⁠ [al-Isra' 110], and so on, at the end of "Glory be to Him" (Subhan), He added further clarity by negating every complete possibility, through His saying: ﴿another﴾. Al-Baghawi said: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "The Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, prostrated in Makkah one night, and he began to say in his prostration: 'O Allah, O Most Merciful.' (p-98) Abu Jahl said: 'Muhammad forbids us from our gods, yet he calls upon two gods!' So Allah revealed this verse, meaning the verse of 'Subhan.'"
