And as a consequence of Our seizing the mockers—and they were the most insolent of them—the rest are threatened by Our saying: ﴿then they will come to know﴾; that is, their knowledge will encompass the severity of Our assault and Our power over what We will; so that it serves as a deterrent to others. Or the mockers and others will come to know the outcome of their affairs in both abodes.

Since his proclamation of this (may God bless him and his family and grant them peace) was accompanied by a great degree of hardship, even though he was relieved of the mockers, because of the large number of those who remained who held the same view as them, He said, consoling him and encouraging him to bear it with patience: ﴿And We certainly know﴾; that is, the occurrence of Our knowledge is established, given the greatness that is Ours; ﴿that you﴾; that is, given the forbearance and the breadth of spirit that are yours; ﴿your breast becomes constricted﴾; that is, its constriction comes into existence and keeps renewing itself; ﴿by what they say﴾; at the time of your declaring to them what you are commanded concerning you, from their saying: "O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down" (Q. 15:6), up to its end; and concerning the One who sent you, from polytheism, and their claims of a consort and a son, and other than that.

﴿فَسَبِّحْ﴾ (So glorify), by reason of that, while ﴿بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ﴾ (with the praise of your Lord), i.e., declare Him free of the attributes of deficiency, among which is heedlessness of what the wrongdoers do, while affirming for Him the attributes of perfection, among which is the exaltation of His ally and the humiliation of His enemy. ﴿وكُنْ﴾ (and be), i.e., with an innate state that never separates from you, ﴿مِنَ السّاجِدِينَ﴾ (among those who prostrate) to Him, i.e., those who pray, i.e., those who are diligent in constant submission to Him through prayer, which is the greatest form of submission to Him, and through other acts of His worship, so that He may suffice you for what concerns you, for there is no sufficer other than Him, and no refuge apart from Him. He expressed this by prostration, indicating its nobility and the supplication that is fitting within it, especially at times of hardship. Indeed, He (Exalted is He) said: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 45]. It is also related that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to turn to prayer whenever a matter distressed him. Al-Baghawi mentioned it without a chain of narration, and it is in the Musnad of Ahmad and the Sunan of Abu Dawud, from Hudhayfah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) used to pray whenever a matter distressed him." In the Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i and the Musnad of Ahmad, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "We saw ourselves on the night of Badr, and there was not a person among us but was asleep, except the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for he was praying beneath a tree and supplicating until morning." In a wording of Ahmad: "We saw ourselves, and there was not a person among us but was asleep, except the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was under a tree praying and weeping until morning." Also in Ahmad, Muslim, and Abu Ya'la, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The closest a servant comes to his Lord is when he is prostrating."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 15, verse 99:

When He commanded him with a particular worship, He followed it with the general worship, saying: ﴿And worship your Lord﴾; that is: persist in the worship of the One who has been good to you through this Qur'an, which is the (means of) conveyance, by the prayer and other (acts); ﴿until the certainty comes to you﴾; by that which expands your breast from death, or what they are promised of the Hour, or other things, by which those who disbelieved will wish, (saying) "If only we had been Muslims." Al-Razi said in "al-Lawami'": This is evidence that the nobility of the servant lies in servanthood, and that worship does not fall from the servant under any circumstance as long as he is alive; end of quote. Al-Baghawi said: This is the meaning of what is in Surah "Maryam" – upon her be peace – ﴿And He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive﴾ [Maryam: 31]. Thus the end of the surah – in the command to take the Qur'an as a conveyance to every good, and in turning away from the disbelievers – corresponds most perfectly to its beginning, and each of the two extremities embraces the other in the most complete embrace; and Allah is the One who grants success to what is right, and to Him is the return and the final resort.
